newsitem.title: USA: L.A. utility hopes to expand affinity mkting deals.
newsitem.headline: L.A. utility hopes to expand affinity mkting deals.

text.p: The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) expects to develop more marketing programs like the wholesale power supply agreement reached with Revelation Corp, an LADWP official said Wednesday.
Revelation, an alliance of the largest African American religious denominations in the U.S., includes 40,000 churches.

Tom McCloskey, LADWP assistant general manager for marketing, said the municipal utility has spent the past year developing a marketing operation aimed at capitalizing on deregulation of the electricity industry.
"We plan to be very aggressive in pursuing new opportunities," he said.

The utility, which now does around $50 million a year in wholesale power trading, hopes to increase revenues from these types of operations so that electricity rates for the city can be kept low, McCloskey said.
LADWP will supply wholesale power to Revelation's new power marketing subisidiary, Revelation Energy Resources, but such sales will be limited until deregulation takes hold nationwide.
So far, New Hamphshire has begun to deregulate its electricity market and the next test market will be in Pennsylvania, where LADWP plans to begin sales in mid-April, McCloskey said.
California will begin phasing out its monopoly utilities next January.
The agreement is not related to LADWP's recently announced plan to form a strategic alliance with power marketer Duke-Louis Dreyfus, McCloskey noted.
But once the alliance is given final approval by the city council, Duke-Louis Dreyfus will "start helping with" the Revelation deal, he said.
